summary: Journal-Fit (EIC) seat. The topic — noise-aware adaptive granular-ball simplification — is within JMLR's scope and the framing is clear, but what is submitted is a four-page sketch rather than a research article: a single mechanism, two baselines, three datasets of which one is private, and no theory, complexity, or variance analysis. As a submission to the stated target venue it is not yet reviewable on quality; the contribution claim outruns what the paper demonstrates.

findings.title: Headline benchmark claim conflicts with the evaluation actually described
findings.detail: The introduction claims a 3.1-point average gain 'across three public benchmarks', but the experiments section names only two public benchmarks plus a private sensor set. Either the claim or the evaluation description is wrong, and in either case a numerate reader cannot reproduce the headline number from the paper. This must be reconciled and the private dataset's provenance, size, and licensing stated.

findings.title: Novelty claim is asserted, not established, and the contribution is thin for the target venue
findings.detail: The paper's entire novelty argument is one sentence dismissing all prior radius selection as global or per-dataset. No prior method is named, compared against, or cited for that claim, and the empirical section contains no adaptive-radius competitor. For JMLR the delta over existing granular-ball and noise-robust simplification work needs to be demonstrated, not asserted.

findings.title: Manuscript is at draft-sketch length with no analysis section
findings.detail: There is no complexity or runtime analysis, no ablation of the mechanism's two components (splitting and merging), no figures, and no discussion section. The target venue expects a full article. I would not send this to referees in its present form, and the author should decide whether the contribution supports a full submission or a short note.
